placements.quote: Since its first light in 2002, H.E.S.S. has provided groundbreaking insights ... The observatory is situated in the Khomas Highland of Namibia at an altitude of 1,800 m

altitude.quote: at about 1,800 m above sea level

telescope_count.quote: H.E.S.S. is a system of five telescopes that are sensitive to high-energy gamma rays ... four 12-meter telescopes, dubbed CT1-4 and installed between 2001 and 2003, are arranged in a square with 120 meter side length. The fifth telescope, CT5, features a 28-meter mirror

description.quote: four 12-meter telescopes, dubbed CT1-4 and installed between 2001 and 2003, are arranged in a square with 120 meter side length.
description.value: Four 12 m diameter imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes (CT1-CT4) arranged in a square of 120 m side length, installed between 2001 and 2003.

description.quote: four 12-m telescopes surrounding a central 28-m telescope — the largest of its kind
description.value: A 28 m diameter telescope (CT5) at the centre of the CT1-CT4 square, described by the collaboration as the largest of its kind; using two telescope sizes enlarges the array's sensitive energy range.

summary.plain: Five telescopes on a Namibian farm: four medium-sized ones in a square around one giant telescope, together watching for the blue flicker of light that gamma rays make hitting the atmosphere.
summary.technical: Hybrid imaging-atmospheric-Cherenkov array: four 12 m telescopes (since 2002) plus a central 28 m telescope (CT5, commissioning date not sourced this session) at 1800 m in the Khomas Highland, Namibia.

technology.quote: four 12-meter telescopes, dubbed CT1-4 and installed between 2001 and 2003, are arranged in a square with 120 meter side length. The fifth telescope, CT5, features a 28-meter mirror ... The H.E.S.S. telescopes are imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, or IACTs.
technology.value: Hybrid array of four 12 m and one 28 m imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes.
